title: Inverse image of the coefficient sheaves
statement:
Because all coefficient sheaves are pulled back from the point, they are compatible with
inverse image. The same holds for their Tate twists ([sk-def-sp-tate-twist]), and a finite
extension of coefficient fields gives a finite free extension of coefficient sheaves.

Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$.
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Coefficient sheaves are the
pullbacks of condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The admissible
coefficients are the finite commutative coefficient rings $A$ and
$\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$. Give $A$ its discrete topology. The rings
$A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$ are condensed as in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; the $\Qlb$ coefficient is specifically
the condensed ring of continuous maps taking values in some finite subextension,
as defined in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed];
$E$ and $F$ below are finite subextensions of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$.
The assertions about Tate twists are made on the domain of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]:
$\ell$ is invertible on $X$ and $Y$, and a finite coefficient ring $A$ being twisted
is annihilated by a power of $\ell$. No such invertibility assumption is imposed
on the untwisted assertions.

1. For every admissible $\Lambda$, the canonical map
   $$
   f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow\Lambda_X
   $$
   is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (this is the map $\alpha_f$
   of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]). For every integer $d$, its Tate twists have the corresponding canonical
   isomorphism of coefficient module sheaves
   $f^{-1}(\Lambda_Y(d))\cong\Lambda_X(d)$ along $\alpha_f$, including the twists
   of a finite ring $A$.
2. If $E\subset F$ is a finite extension, then $\cO_{F,X}$ is a finite free
   $\cO_{E,X}$-module and $F_X$ is a finite free $E_X$-module.

By (1), the pullback $f^*\colon\Mod(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
of modules over these sheaves is exact. More precisely, it is canonically naturally
isomorphic to the lift of $f^{-1}$ whose underlying sheaf functor is $f^{-1}$
and whose $\Lambda_X$-action is obtained using $\alpha_f^{-1}$.

proof.text: For every admissible $\Lambda$, $\alpha_f$ is the ring-object isomorphism of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], and its invertibility is [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. This proves the untwisted part of (1).
When $\ell$ is invertible on $X,Y$, [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] gives $f^{-1}\Lambda_Y(d)\cong\Lambda_X(d)$ along $\alpha_f$, for all $d$, including finite $\ell$-power-torsion $A$.

Choose an integral basis for $E\subset F$ by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. Then [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free] identifies $\mathcal O_{F,X}$ and $F_X$ with $d=[F:E]$ copies of their respective base rings, proving (2).

Use the small sites of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Their abelian sheaf categories are abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], hence have equalizers and coequalizers. The tensor is closed symmetric monoidal by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], additive and colimit-preserving by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-closed]. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applies to the rings $\Lambda_X,\Lambda_Y$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients].

By [def-sfb-module-upper-star], $f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{-1})$. The source ring is commutative by $\alpha_f$. Steps 1 and 4 allow [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso], giving $f^*\cong G:=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f^{-1}}\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{-1})$. The action is $\widetilde\gamma\circ(\alpha_f^{-1}\otimes1)$. Both factors commute with forgetful functors by [sk-def-sfb-transport] and [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]; hence $U_XG=f^{-1}U_Y$.

proof.text: View abelian sheaves as internal group objects by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebraic-structures-objects]. Clauses 3–4 of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] compute abelian inverse image on the finite-limit-preserving set inverse image. By [lem-sfb-internal-abelian-finite-limit-creation], its transported group functor preserves finite limits. In particular it preserves binary products and the terminal abelian sheaf, which is zero. Zero arrows factor through zero. Thus [lem-sfb-products-zero-additive] makes abelian inverse image additive.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, abelian-group part; final exactness sentence of the blueprint item, refined via the new finite-limit creation statement.

proof.text: Abelian $f^{-1}$ is exact by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image]. Steps 4–6 verify all hypotheses of [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] for $F=f^{-1}$ and the lift $G$: abelian ambient categories, additive right-exact tensors, additive exact $F$, and $U_XG=FU_Y$. Therefore $G$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

source.place: final exactness sentence: apply exact lifting

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-exactness-nat-iso] to the inverse of the comparison $f^*\cong G$ from step 5. Thus $f^*$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits, as asserted; its specified comparison with $G$ supplies the canonical identification. All untwisted steps apply without inverting $\ell$ on $X,Y$.
